title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which scammers used AI-generated deepfake video and fake social media profiles to present themselves as a real, named immigration attorney. The failure sits entirely outside any legitimate AI deployment, the technology was used by third-party criminals rather than misused by a company or product. The harm occurred at the point of contact between victims and fraudulent accounts on major social media platforms, where users had no straightforward way to distinguish fabricated video from authentic content.

The scale is concrete: nearly 6,500 fake profiles were identified and removed across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram before the platforms acted on them. Detection came not from platform moderation but from the attorney's own firm hiring an anti-piracy company, meaning the social media systems did not catch the impersonation at the point of publication. A verification layer that matched accounts claiming to represent licensed professionals against authoritative records could have flagged the volume of duplicate identities, but no such check is reported to have existed or been triggered here.

What is not established is who is responsible for operating the scheme, where the scammers are located, or whether any platform failed a specific legal or policy obligation, none of those questions has been resolved by the reporting.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of AI-powered scammers who are using deepfake videos and fake social media profiles featuring his likeness to defraud vulnerable immigrants. The criminals are offering fraudulent immigration services through hundreds of fake accounts, including promises of US residency for $2,200 and claims of help obtaining legal status. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began contacting his office about services he never provided. The situation has escalated dramatically over the past three months, with scammers directing victims through WhatsApp to send money via payment apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App.

An anti-piracy company hired by Leal's firm has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 on TikTok, 2,400 on Facebook, and 544 on Instagram. The fraudulent videos also feature fake testimonials from supposed clients praising Leal's services. Leal is warning immigrants to verify identities of legal service providers and be suspicious of immediate payment requests, emphasizing that his office never requests payments over the phone. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to investigate the source of the scams.
